haiku-low.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. It never calls Redis, so no rate-limit counter is read or changed.
haiku-low.q2: Standard customers get 100 per minute total. All of a customer's keys share one budget, so the three keys do not multiply it.
haiku-low.q3: 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header. The request is never forwarded, so the backend never sees it.
haiku-low.q4: No. A denied request changes nothing in the counter store, so the 429 costs no budget.
haiku-low.q5: Yes. The request is counted before forwarding, so it uses budget even when the backend returns 500.
haiku-low.q6: The request is forwarded anyway, the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric is emitted, and the response has no X-RateLimit headers.
haiku-low.q7: Standard: 100 requests per minute. Enterprise: ENTERPRISE_LIMIT, which has no default and is not yet set by Product.
haiku-low.q8: In a shared Redis counter store (primary with replica), under key rl:{customerId}:{windowNumber}. Keys expire about 60 seconds after their window ends.
haiku-low.q9: Each clock-minute window starts its count at 0, so the budget resets when a new minute window begins.
haiku-low.q10: The check and increment run as one atomic Lua script on Redis, so no other command can run between the read and the increment.
haiku-low.q11: Retry-After = max(1, 60 - (now mod 60)), where now is Redis time in seconds. It is the time until the current window ends.
haiku-low.q12: Retry: NOT STATED. The client gets the normal backend response with no X-RateLimit-* headers.

sonnet.q1: The gateway returns 401 Unauthorized. It never calls Redis, so no counter is read or changed.
sonnet.q2: The budget belongs to the customer, so all its keys share it: the customer's single per-minute limit in total (100 if Standard; Enterprise limit not decided).
sonnet.q3: A 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header (whole seconds). The backend never sees the request; it is not forwarded.
sonnet.q4: No. The script changes nothing when denied, so a 429 costs no budget.
sonnet.q5: Yes. The request was already counted, so it uses budget even if the backend returns 500.
sonnet.q6: Fail open: the gateway forwards the request anyway and emits the ratelimit_store_unavailable metric. The client gets the normal backend response without X-RateLimit headers. A late reply is ignored.
sonnet.q7: Standard is 100 per minute. Enterprise is not decided; it comes from the configured ENTERPRISE_LIMIT, which has no default (Product hasn't set it).
sonnet.q8: In the shared Redis counter store (primary with replica), under key rl:{customerId}:{windowNumber}. Old counts expire by themselves: the key is set to expire about 60 seconds after its window ends.
sonnet.q9: Each fixed one-minute clock window has its own count starting at 0, so the budget resets when the next window begins (Redis time in seconds divided by 60, rounded down).
sonnet.q10: The check-and-increment runs as a Redis Lua script, which executes as a single step with no other command in the middle, so two gateways cannot both read 99 and both allow.
sonnet.q11: Retry-After = max(1, 60 - (now mod 60)) in whole seconds, where now is Redis time in seconds; i.e. time until the current window ends.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED whether it retries the store (the document describes forwarding without any retry). The client gets no rate-limit information: no X-RateLimit-* headers, just the normal backend response.
